metadata.title: On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma

nodes.name: $1$-sub-Gaussian random variable
nodes.statement: A random variable $X$ is $1$-sub-Gaussian if $\forall \lambda \in \R, \E[e^{\lambda X}] \leq e^{\lambda^2/2}$. This implies $\E[X]=0$ and $\Var[X] \leq 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: X is 1-sub-Gaussian when its moment generating function is dominated by that of a standard Gaussian.

nodes.name: $1$-sub-Gaussian random vector
nodes.statement: A random vector $X \in \R^n$ is $1$-sub-Gaussian if for any $u \in \R^d$, $\E[e^{u^T X}] \leq \exp(\|u\|_2^2/2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Vector version: MGF dominated by a standard Gaussian's MGF.

nodes.name: $q$-sparse random matrix
nodes.statement: A random matrix with independent entries is $q$-sparse if each coefficient has probability at least $1-q$ to be equal to zero.
nodes.statement_clean: Each entry is zero with probability at least 1-q.

nodes.name: $(\kappa,\kappa',s)$-full vector
nodes.statement: For $\kappa<\kappa' \in (0,1)$ and integer $s \in \{1,\dots,p\}$, a vector $v$ is $(\kappa,\kappa',s)$-full if $\|v\|_\infty \leq \sqrt{\kappa'/s}$ and $|\{k : |v_k| \geq \sqrt{\kappa/s}\}| \geq s$.
nodes.statement_clean: A vector that has at least s coordinates of comparable size and bounded sup-norm.

nodes.name: Achlioptas' distribution
nodes.statement: $P = \frac{q}{2}\delta_{-1/\sqrt{q}} + (1-q)\delta_0 + \frac{q}{2}\delta_{1/\sqrt{q}}$, with the canonical choice $q=1/3$.
nodes.statement_clean: Three-point sparse distribution centered at zero, used as random projection entries.

nodes.name: Sparse projection matrix $A$
nodes.statement: $A_{ik} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{dq}}\zeta_{ik} U_{ik}$ where $U \in \R^{d \times p}$ has iid $1$-sub-Gaussian variance-$1$ entries and $\zeta \in \R^{d \times p}$ has iid $\mathrm{Bern}(q)$ entries independent of $U$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bernoulli-masked sub-Gaussian matrix used as a sparse random projection.

nodes.name: Random projection (dimensionality reduction)
nodes.statement: Given $x_1,\dots,x_n \in \R^p$ and tolerance $\epsilon>0$, find a matrix $A \in \mathcal{M}_{d,p}(\R)$ with small $d$ such that $(1-\epsilon)\|Ax_i-Ax_j\|^2 \leq \|x_i-x_j\|^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|Ax_i-Ax_j\|^2$ for all $1\leq i,j\leq n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Embed n high-dimensional points into low dimension while approximately preserving pairwise distances.

nodes.name: Quasi-isometry property
nodes.statement: $\forall 1\leq i,j\leq n,\ (1-\epsilon)\|Ax_i-Ax_j\|^2 \leq \|x_i-x_j\|^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|Ax_i-Ax_j\|^2$.

nodes.name: Classical JL dimension condition
nodes.statement: $d \geq \frac{8\log(n)}{\epsilon^2 - \epsilon^3}$.

nodes.name: Gaussian-trick exponential moment identity
nodes.statement: For any $x \in \R$ and $\ell>0$, $e^{\ell x^2} = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{\lambda x}\frac{e^{-\lambda^2/(4\ell)}}{2\sqrt{\pi\ell}}\,d\lambda$, equivalently $\E_X[e^{\ell X^2}] \leq \E_G[e^{\ell G^2}] = 1/\sqrt{1-2\ell}$ for $G \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Deviation bound for averages of squared sub-Gaussians
nodes.statement: If $X_1,\dots,X_d$ are iid $1$-sub-Gaussian with variance $1$, then $\P\left(\frac{X_1^2+\dots+X_d^2}{d} \notin [1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon]\right) \leq 2 e^{-d(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/4}$.

nodes.name: Optimal sparsity of $1$-sub-Gaussian variance-$1$ laws (Achlioptas optimality)
nodes.statement: If $X$ is a $1$-sub-Gaussian random variable of variance $1$, then $\P(X=0) \leq 2/3$, with equality iff $\P(X=-\sqrt{3}) = \P(X=\sqrt{3}) = \P(X \neq 0)/2$.

nodes.name: Hanson-Wright inequality for non-negative quadratic forms
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a $d \times d$ symmetric matrix with non-negative eigenvalues and $X$ a $1$-sub-Gaussian vector. Then for any $\ell \in [0, 1/(2\|S\|_{op}))$, $\E_X[e^{\ell X^T S X}] \leq \exp\left(\ell\Tr(S) + \frac{\ell^2 \|S\|_F^2}{1-2\ell\|S\|_{op}}\right)$.
assumptions: $S$ is $d \times d$ symmetric with non-negative eigenvalues

nodes.name: Right-tail Chernoff bound (squared sub-Gaussian)
nodes.statement: $\P\left(\frac{Z_1+\dots+Z_d}{d} \geq 1+\epsilon\right) \leq e^{-d(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/4}$, where $Z_i = X_i^2$ with $X_i$ iid $1$-sub-Gaussian variance-$1$.

nodes.name: Left-tail Chernoff bound (squared sub-Gaussian)
nodes.statement: $\P\left(\frac{Z_1+\dots+Z_d}{d} \leq 1-\epsilon\right) \leq e^{-d(\epsilon^2/4 - 3\epsilon^3/16)} \leq e^{-d(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/4}$.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma (sub-Gaussian version)
nodes.statement: For any $x_1,\dots,x_n \in \R^p$ and $\epsilon>0$, if $d \geq \frac{8\log(n)}{\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3}$ then there exists $A \in \mathcal{M}_{d,p}(\R)$ such that $(1-\epsilon)\|Ax_i-Ax_j\|^2 \leq \|x_i-x_j\|^2 \leq (1+\epsilon)\|Ax_i-Ax_j\|^2$ for all $1 \leq i,j \leq n$.
conclusions: There exists $A \in \mathcal{M}_{d,p}(\R)$ achieving the $\epsilon$-quasi-isometry on all $\binom{n}{2}$ pairs

nodes.name: Sparse JL with target dimension $\Theta(\log n / \epsilon^2)$
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\dots,x_n \in \R^p$, $\epsilon>0$. For $d \geq \frac{36 \log(2n^2)}{\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3}$ and $q \geq \max_{i\neq j}\frac{18\|x_i-x_j\|_4^4 + 2\|x_i-x_j\|_\infty^2 \|x_i-x_j\|_2^2}{\epsilon^2 \|x_i-x_j\|_2^4}\log(2d)$, the $\epsilon$-quasi-isometry holds with positive probability.

nodes.name: High-probability sparse JL with poly-log target dimension
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\dots,x_n \in \R^p$ and $A \in \R^{d\times p}$ with $A_{ik}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{dq}}\zeta_{ik}U_{ik}$, $q \geq \max_{i\neq j}\frac{\|x_i-x_j\|_\infty^2}{\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2}$. For any $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $d \geq \frac{12}{\epsilon^2}\log(3n/\delta)\big(1+\sqrt{4\log(nd/\delta)}+2\log(nd/\delta)\big)^2$, the $\epsilon$-quasi-isometry holds with probability $\geq 1-\delta$.
assumptions: $A_{ik} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{dq}}\zeta_{ik}U_{ik}$ with iid Bernoulli mask and iid $1$-sub-Gaussian variance-$1$ $U_{ik}$

nodes.name: Optimality of the sparsity threshold $q \gtrsim 1/s$
nodes.statement: Let $A \in \R^{d\times p}$ have iid coefficients from Achlioptas' distribution with parameter $q$, and $y \in \R^p$ a unit vector with coordinates in $\{-1/\sqrt{s},1/\sqrt{s},0\}$. If $dqs\epsilon^2 \leq 1/2$ and $qs < 1/240$, then $\P(\|Ay\|^2 \in [1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon]) \leq 1 - e^{-5000}$.
assumptions: $A$ has iid Achlioptas-distributed coefficients with parameter $q$
$y \in \R^p$ is a unit vector with coordinates in $\{-1/\sqrt{s}, 1/\sqrt{s}, 0\}$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition $\ref{prop:devX2}$ (deviation of squared sub-Gaussians)
nodes.statement: Split into right- and left-deviation Chernoff arguments using the Gaussian-trick identity for the upper tail and a Taylor-bound on $\E[X^4] \leq 3$ for the lower tail.

nodes.name: Right-tail moment bound via Gaussian trick
nodes.statement: Show that for $\ell \in (0,1/2)$, $\E[e^{\ell X^2}] \leq 1/\sqrt{1-2\ell}$ using $e^{\ell x^2} = \int e^{\lambda x} e^{-\lambda^2/(4\ell)}/(2\sqrt{\pi\ell})\,d\lambda$ and Fubini.

nodes.name: Right-tail Chernoff optimization
nodes.statement: Apply Markov to $e^{\ell(Z_1+\dots+Z_d)}$, optimize $\ell^* = \epsilon/(2(1+\epsilon))$, and use Pollard's trick to get $I(\epsilon) \geq (\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/4$, yielding (\ref{eq:chernoffUB}).

nodes.name: Left-tail moment bound via Taylor
nodes.statement: Use $\Var[X]=1$ and sub-Gaussianity to get $\E[X^4] \leq 3$. Then $\E[e^{-\ell X^2}] \leq 1 - \ell + 3\ell^2/2$ via $e^{-u} \leq 1-u+u^2/2$.

nodes.name: Left-tail Chernoff optimization
nodes.statement: Apply Markov, choose $\ell = \epsilon/2$, and bound to obtain $\P\big(\bar Z_d \leq 1-\epsilon\big) \leq e^{-d(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/4}$, yielding (\ref{eq:chernoffLB}).

nodes.name: Proof of the classical JL Lemma (Theorem $\ref{thm:classicalJL}$)
nodes.statement: Take $A_{ij}=T_{ij}/\sqrt{d}$ with $T_{ij}$ iid centered $1$-sub-Gaussian variance $1$; show $Z_i := \sqrt{d}\,(Ay)_i/\|y\|$ is $1$-sub-Gaussian; apply Proposition $\ref{prop:devX2}$ and a union bound.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussianity of normalized projection
nodes.statement: Show $Z_i = \sum_j (y_j/\|y\|) T_{ij}$ is $1$-sub-Gaussian by independence and the $1$-sub-Gaussian assumption on each $T_{ij}$.

nodes.name: Apply concentration of squared sub-Gaussians
nodes.statement: Use Proposition $\ref{prop:devX2}$ on $Z_i^2$ to get $\P(\|Ay\|^2/\|y\|^2 \notin [1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon]) \leq 2 e^{-d(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/4} \leq 2/n^2$ for $d \geq 8\log(n)/(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)$.

nodes.name: Union bound over pairs
nodes.statement: By the union bound over the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairs, the probability of failure is $< n(n-1)/n^2 < 1$, so a valid $A$ exists by the probabilistic method.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition $\ref{prop:ArchiBest}$
nodes.statement: Decompose $X = \zeta U$ with $\zeta \sim \mathrm{Bern}(q)$; use $\E[X^4] \leq 3$ and Cauchy-Schwarz $\E[U^4] \geq \E[U^2]^2$ to deduce $q \geq 1/3$. Verify the equality case by checking the MGF inequality termwise.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition $\ref{prop:right_tail}$ (Hanson-Wright for non-negative quadratic forms)
nodes.statement: Diagonalize $S = P\,\Diag(\mu_i)\,P^T$, set $Y = PX$ (still $1$-sub-Gaussian), apply the Gaussian-trick (\ref{eq:gaussianTrick}) coordinate-wise to get $\E[e^{\ell X^T S X}] \leq \E_G[e^{\sum_i \ell\mu_i G_i^2/2}] = \prod_i 1/\sqrt{1-2\ell\mu_i}$, then use $-\tfrac12\log(1-2\ell\mu_i)-\ell\mu_i \leq \ell^2\mu_i^2/(1-2\ell\mu_i)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem $\ref{thm:JLs1s}$ (sparse JL, $\Theta(\log n/\epsilon^2)$)
nodes.statement: Condition on the mask $\zeta$ and decompose into a typical event $G$ on $\sum_k (y_k^2/q)\zeta_{ik}$ controlled by Bernstein, then apply (\ref{eq:gaussianTrick}) and the Chernoff bounds (\ref{eq:chernoffUB}), (\ref{eq:chernoffLB}) on $G$.

nodes.name: Define and control the typical mask event $G_i$
nodes.statement: Let $G_i = \{(1-\epsilon/3)\|y\|_2^2 \leq \sum_k (y_k^2/q)\zeta_{ik} \leq (1+\epsilon/3)\|y\|_2^2\}$. By Bernstein's inequality, $\P(\bar G_i) \leq 2\exp\big(-q\epsilon^2\|y\|_2^4/(18\|y\|_4^4 + 2\|y\|_\infty^2\|y\|_2^2)\big) \leq 1/(2d)$ when (\ref{eq:qmin}) holds.

nodes.name: Conditional sub-Gaussianity on $G_i$
nodes.statement: On $G_i$, $\E[e^{\lambda Z_i}\1_{G_i}] \leq \exp(\lambda^2(1+\epsilon/3)/2)$, so $Z_i/\sqrt{1+\epsilon/3}$ is $1$-sub-Gaussian conditionally; then $\E[e^{\ell Z_i^2/(1+\epsilon/3)}\1_{G_i}] \leq 1/\sqrt{1-2\ell}$.

nodes.name: Conclude via Chernoff and union bound
nodes.statement: On $G = \bigcap_i G_i$, apply (\ref{eq:chernoffUB})-(\ref{eq:chernoffLB}) to get $\P(G \cap \{\|Ay\|^2/\|y\|^2 \notin [1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon]\}) \leq 2 e^{-d(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/36}$. A union bound over $\binom{n}{2}$ pairs gives total failure probability $< 1/2 + n^2 e^{-d(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)/36} \leq 1$ for $d \geq 36\log(2n^2)/(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem $\ref{th:jl_sparse}$ (high-probability sparse JL)
nodes.statement: Write $A = \zeta \odot U/\sqrt{dq}$ and $w_i = \zeta_{i\cdot}\odot y/\sqrt{dq}$; bound $\E_U[e^{\ell Y_i^2}]$ via Hanson-Wright-type estimate and the event $G = \{\max_i \|w_i\|^2 \leq \Psi/d\}$ controlled by Bernstein; combine with a separate fourth-moment argument for the lower tail.

nodes.name: Conditional MGF bound for $Y_i^2$
nodes.statement: Conditionally on $\zeta$, $Y_i/\|w_i\|$ is $1$-sub-Gaussian. For $\ell \in [0,1/(2\max\|w_i\|^2))$, $\E_U[e^{\ell Y_i^2}] \leq 1/\sqrt{1-2\ell\|w_i\|^2} \leq \exp\big(\ell\|w_i\|^2 + \ell^2\|w_i\|^4/(1-2\ell\|w_i\|^2)\big)$.

nodes.name: Bernstein control of $\max_i \|w_i\|^2$ and event $G$
nodes.statement: By Bernstein and a union bound over $i \in [d]$, with probability $\geq 1-\delta/(3n^2)$ the event $G = \{\max_i \|w_i\|^2 \leq \Psi/d\}$ holds where $\Psi = 1+\sqrt{4\log(3nd/\delta)} + 2\log(3nd/\delta)$.

nodes.name: Bound $\E[\exp(\ell\sum_i\|w_i\|^2)]$
nodes.statement: Using $e^u \leq 1+u+(e-2)u^2$ on $[0,1]$, $\E[\exp(\ell\sum_i\|w_i\|^2)] \leq \exp(\ell + (e-2)\ell^2/d)$ for $\ell \in [0, dq/\|y\|_\infty^2)$.

nodes.name: Optimize $\ell$ for upper deviation
nodes.statement: Choosing $\ell = d\epsilon/(2(e-2)+4\Psi^2)$ gives $\P(\|Ay\|^2 \geq 1+\epsilon) \leq e^{-d\epsilon^2/(2(e-2)+4\Psi^2)} + \delta/(3n^2) \leq 2\delta/(3n^2)$ for $d \geq 12\log(3n/\delta)\Psi^2/\epsilon^2$.

nodes.name: Lower-tail fourth-moment bound
nodes.statement: Bound $\E[(Ay)_i^4] \leq 6/d^2$ directly. Then $\P(\|Ay\|^2 \leq 1-\epsilon) \leq \exp(3\ell^2/d - \ell\epsilon) \leq \exp(-d\epsilon^2/12)$ at $\ell=\epsilon/6$.

nodes.name: Union bound and combine
nodes.statement: Two union bounds over $\binom{n}{2}$ pairs combined give the $\epsilon$-quasi-isometry property with probability $\geq 1-\delta$ when $d \geq d_0$ and $q$ satisfies (\ref{eq:condition_q}).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem $\ref{th:optimality}$ (optimality of sparsity threshold)
nodes.statement: Two regimes. If $dqs \leq 1/2048$, $\P(Ay = 0) \geq e^{-ds q/(1-q)} \geq e^{-5000}$. Otherwise, apply Chebyshev with explicit moments of order 2, 4, 6, 8 of $\|Ay\|$.

nodes.name: Trivial regime $dqs \leq 1/2048$
nodes.statement: $\P(\|Ay\|^2 \notin [1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon]) \geq \P(Ay=0) \geq e^{-ds q/(1-q)} \geq e^{-5000}$, giving the bound.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $\E[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2]$
nodes.statement: Compute $\E[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2] = \frac{1}{dqs} + \frac{3}{d}(1-1/s) + \frac{d-1}{d} - 1 + \dots \geq \frac{1}{dqs}$ via index-matching combinatorics on $A_{ik}$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $\Var[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2]$
nodes.statement: Decompose $\E[\|Ay\|^8]$ over five index-pattern sets $I_1,\dots,I_5$ to bound it by $1 + 6/(dqs) + 18/d + 253/(d^2q^2s^2)$. Combined with a lower bound on $\E[\|Ay\|^6]$, get $\Var[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2] \leq 256/(d^2q^2s^2) + 30/d$.

nodes.name: Apply Chebyshev
nodes.statement: Chebyshev: $\P(\|Ay\|^2 \in [1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon]) \leq \Var[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2]/(\E[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2]-\epsilon^2) \leq (256/(dqs) + 30 qs)/(1-dqs\epsilon^2) \leq 1/2$ under the assumptions.

nodes.name: Optimal constant in JL condition
nodes.statement: The constant $8$ in $d \geq 8\log(n)/(\epsilon^2-\epsilon^3)$ is the best obtainable from this proof. The Gaussian case admits $d = 4\log(n)/(\epsilon-\log(1+\epsilon)) \leq 8\log(n)(1+\epsilon/3)^2/\epsilon^2$.

nodes.name: $1$-sub-Gaussian variance-$1$ examples
nodes.statement: Examples include the symmetric Bernoulli $P=(\delta_{-1}+\delta_1)/2$ and the uniform $P=\mathcal{U}([-\sqrt{3},\sqrt{3}])$, both with MGFs bounded by $e^{\lambda^2/2}$. Another example: $P = \frac{1}{12}\delta_{-2} + \frac{1}{6}\delta_{-1} + \frac{1}{2}\delta_0 + \frac{1}{6}\delta_{1} + \frac{1}{12}\delta_{2}$.

nodes.name: Sufficient sparsity from $(\kappa,\kappa',s)$-fullness
nodes.statement: If all differences $x_i-x_j$ are $(\kappa,\kappa',s)$-full, then $q \geq (\kappa'/\kappa)/s$ suffices; in the dense case ($s=p$) this gives $q \gtrsim 1/p$, much smaller than $1/3$ when $p \gg 1/\epsilon^2$.

nodes.name: Concentration consequence of Hanson-Wright (Section 4)
nodes.statement: Following Theorem 10 of Boucheron et al. (2013), Proposition $\ref{prop:right_tail}$ implies with probability $\geq 1-\delta$, $X^T S X \leq \Tr(S) + \sqrt{4\|S\|_F^2 \log(1/\delta)} + 2\|S\|_{op}\log(1/\delta)$.

nodes.name: Sparse JL experiment with Gaussian data (full)
nodes.statement: $n$ data points $x_i \in \R^{10000}$ with iid Gaussian coordinates, target $d=500$, projection entries $\frac{q}{2}\delta_{-1/\sqrt{dq}} + (1-q)\delta_0 + \frac{q}{2}\delta_{1/\sqrt{dq}}$. Empirically, $q=1/3$ plays no special role; sparser projections also preserve distances.

nodes.name: Sparse JL with $s$-sparse data (Figure 2)
nodes.statement: Each $x_i \in \R^{10000}$ has exactly $s$ non-zero independent Gaussian entries; same projection scheme as above. Quasi-isometry holds whenever $q \times s$ is sufficiently large.

nodes.name: Effect of varying $q$ for fixed sparsity (Figure 3)
nodes.statement: $n=100$ points $x_i \in \R^{10000}$ with $\pm 1$ coordinates non-zero with probability $s/p$; $q \geq 1/3$ ensures the quasi-isometry uniformly, while smaller $q$ requires $s \gtrsim 1/q$.

nodes.name: Bernstein's inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For independent bounded random variables $X_k \in [0, b]$ with $\sum_k \Var(X_k) \leq v$, $\P(\sum_k (X_k - \E X_k) \geq t) \leq \exp(-t^2/(2v + 2bt/3))$.

nodes.name: Chebyshev's inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For a non-negative random variable $Y$ and $a > 0$, $\P(Y \geq a) \leq \E[Y]/a$; equivalently for $|Y - \E Y|^2$, used here as $\P(|\|Ay\|^2 - 1| \leq \epsilon) \leq \Var[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2]/(\E[(\|Ay\|^2-1)^2] - \epsilon^2)$.
